epic:#27261#1 · marchtian · session_017ihL2c5z3q4h8inrn5kwqV

A Tier A reading that bears on this decision, carried here, not filed (from the #27278 dev report 6485876530; seam-level probe at `origin/main` 6d7634a9, not measured at a public door):

- For a datasource whose driver a plugin already registered (`driver.<name>` service), `DatasourceConnectionService` returns `already-registered` before credential resolution: `external.credentialsRef` is not resolved, not handed to the driver, and does not fail the boot when no secret store is configured (0 resolver calls, with and without a secret store). A driver that is not pre-registered resolves it (1 resolver call).
- So today a plugin driver gets its credential from the options the host passes to the plugin, and the "credentials only through `credentialsRef`" rule of ruling 6471382887 is not what Tier A does. The guide (PR #27349, `content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx` § Credentials) states this behaviour as it is.
- The dev's options: (A) the platform hands the resolved `credentialsRef` to a plugin driver; (B) bless host-composed plugin options as the Tier A channel and amend the rule; (C) refuse at boot a `credentialsRef` on a plugin-registered driver's datasource, so it is never silently ignored. Whatever this card rules for API-backed datasources should settle the plugin-driver case in the same ruling.

Director seat, summon #54 (ledger objectstack#12708, opening mark 6485456694). Presented to the maintainer in batch #426 as item 1 of 3, together with its sibling #27299 and #27302 (one family: epics #27261 / #27293).

Seat increment (re-read at `origin/main` `73725c20`, 2026-10-29T02:14Z):
- Premises re-run, all hold: `REF_PREFIX = 'sys_secret:'` at datasource-secret-binder.ts L21; `defaultEnvCredentialResolver` at credential-resolver.ts L21; `credentialsRef` in 39 non-test source files, `credentialRef` in 19; ADR-0143 "bound to `(organization, connector instance)`" L300, Q1 "Decision (2026-10-28): A." L283; ADR-0015 `credentialsRef` L13 / L204 / L625.
- Prior rulings: `check-prior-rulings.mjs --card 27298` names ADR-0143 D1 / D3 (the tier line; secrets are references, tokens live in a connection record), ADR-0023 §4, ADR-0022 §4, ADR-0024 §4 — none decides how a datasource reaches a connector's credential. Thread: #27261 ruling 6471382887 D1 / D2 and its standing rule "credentials only through `credentialsRef`", which this card asks to amend for API-backed datasources; #27230 ruled A on connector static secrets only. The epic body (#27261 §4 item 8) still reads "Credentials: only `external.credentialsRef`" — amended by this ruling if A or B.
- Facets: agree with the card on all four. ① one vendor, one grant, used for actions and for reading — the Dataverse connection-reference / Salesforce Named Credential shape. ③ decides against C: an author writes a static key for an OAuth source and gets a runtime 401; A refuses at build when the named instance does not exist. ④ A is one optional key.
- Seat's letter: **A** — the datasource's `external` block names a declared connector instance and borrows its credential through ADR-0143 D4's per-dispatch resolver; execution identity stays ADR-0143 Q1 = A (organization-shared). Not B (two grants per vendor), not C (closes Tier B to OAuth sources). Nothing is dispatched now: implementation rides P2's children, filed on the second pull (D1).
- Workload of A: `domain:spec` 1 PR (S, one key + an ADR-0015 amendment note, Tier H) + `domain:server` 1 PR (S–M, the shared resolver seam) · at P2 · no precedent. Confidence gap kept from the card: whether the `objectql`-side driver reaches the automation service's resolver without a new dependency direction (may cost one more small spec PR), and whether the connection record's `(organization, connector instance)` binding fits an environment-level datasource (#27230 S1).
- After the ruling: the epic PM records it as D7 on #27261; this card then leaves the box (`pm:blocked` behind P2's gate, or closed with the pointer, the epic PM's call under `pm:epic`).

Prior rulings read: datasource, connector, credential, OAuth, credentialsRef → ADR-0143 D1 / D3 / D4 / Q1 / Q2, ADR-0015 §10; thread: 6471382887 (#27261), #27230 A; repo: objectstack-ai/objectstack

director#1 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbQLcy8yg6vhJVXXi8

Ruling: batch #426 item 1 · letter A · maintainer 「同意」 2026-10-29T02:22Z

Director seat, summon #54 (ledger objectstack#12708, opening mark 6485456694, brief 6486018608). The maintainer answered batch #426 in the summon chat with one word, verbatim: 「同意」 — the seat's letter on each of the three cards; for this card **A**.

**What the ruling binds (letter A):** an API-backed external datasource authenticates by naming a declared connector instance in its `external` block and borrowing that instance's credential — static, `oauth2`, `app-credential` and `signed` kinds alike — through ADR-0143 D4's per-dispatch resolver. One Connect per vendor serves both actions (flows) and records (virtual objects); a reconnect fixes both. The key is one optional member of the datasource `external` block, refused at build when the named instance is not declared (`Metadata-protocol: added`, filed with P2). Execution identity is not reopened: ADR-0143 Q1 = A (organization-shared) applies to the virtual-object read as to the flow dispatch; object permissions and RLS stay the only gate on what a user sees (#27261 §5.9). **Amendment recorded:** #27261 ruling 6471382887's standing rule "credentials only through `credentialsRef`" and the epic body's §4 item 8 now read: through `credentialsRef`, or through a declared connector instance for an API-backed datasource. Not taken: B (a second grant per vendor, a second Connect flow, drift between two auth blocks), C (a static key for OAuth sources, runtime 401).

Governing text: ADR-0143 D3 / D4 / Q1 A / Q2 B; ADR-0015 §10; ruling 6471382887 D1 / D2 on #27261; #27230 ruled A (connector static secrets). Premises re-read at `origin/main` `73725c20` (brief 6486018608).

**Workload of the letter:** `domain:spec` 1 PR (S: the key plus an ADR-0015 amendment note, Tier H) + `domain:server` 1 PR (S–M: the shared resolver seam) · no UI · filed with P2 on the second customer pull (D1), not now · no precedent. Open readings for P2's spec child: whether the `objectql`-side driver reaches the automation service's resolver without a new dependency direction; whether the `(organization, connector instance)` binding fits an environment-level datasource (#27230 S1).

**Execution:** nothing is dispatched. The epic PM of #27261 records this as **D7** in the epic body and corrects §4 item 8; this card closes `completed` in this act (the ruling is its content; P2's children cite this comment on a `Ruling-ref:` line when filed).
